title: streaming-sse-chunking-backpressure-debug-notes
content:
Scratchpad: debugging streaming SSE / chunking / backpressure issues

Summary:
- Intermittent streaming stalls and truncated streams observed from hosted API when clients use SSE or chunked responses over long outputs (~>2k tokens).
- Symptoms: client receives initial tokens, then stream pauses for 5-30s, then either resumes with a burst of buffered tokens or terminates with a chunked-transfer EOF. Sometimes duplicate tokens appear.
- Happens more often for multi-tenant host pool under moderate load and for longer context lengths. Dev-local and Dedicated with isolated GPUs rare.

What I've tried so far (commands + notes):

1) Reproduce with curl (raw SSE)
- curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.internal/v1/streams?model=redwood-medium&prompt=long_story"
Notes: -v shows socket open; we see initial SSE events, then no data for ~12s, then a chunk arrives. -N (no-buffer) required.

2) Node fetch streaming test (ReadableStream)
- node reproduction/snippets/stream-client.js (attached gist in GH PR)
Observed: Node stream 'data' events stop, 'end' only after server EOS or connection closed.

3) Python requests (stream=True)
- python3 repro/stream_test.py --model redwood-medium --prompt-file long_prompt.txt
Observed: requests.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True) stops yielding for a while. Confirmed same pause behavior.

4) Localserver mock to compare behavior (netcat / python aiohttp)
- Started an aiohttp SSE server that flushes every token with await resp.write(f"data: {token}\n\n") and flush. Local clients show smooth streaming (no pauses). Suggests problem upstream (proxy/load balancer) not application code.

5) Bypassed internal load balancer / proxy by hitting backend node on private IP (port-forward)
- curl directly to backend: much smoother, fewer pauses. Strong hint: proxy or gateway introducing buffering/backpressure.

6) tcpdump + Wireshark
- Observed that server sends small TCP segments but there are long gaps where intermediaries ACK but not forward to client (or vice versa). Also saw PSH flags behavior inconsistent.

7) Experimented with Transfer-Encoding headers
- Forcing 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' vs explicit Content-Length (not possible for streaming) but observed that when response includes 'Connection: keep-alive' and chunked encoding, some proxies buffer until chunks > X bytes.

8) Nginx / envoy hypotheses
- Envoy has HTTP/1.1 HTTP2 transitions and may buffer if 'proxy_buffering on' or due to per-connection flow control windows.
- Nginx default proxy_buffering can cause buffering of chunked SSE until buffer fills.

9) Repro variants that change behavior:
- Sending larger token payloads less likely to pause (suggests threshold-based buffering).
- Enabling trailing colon comments (':keepalive') every 15s keeps connection alive but does not always prevent pauses.

Error snippets / logs:
- Client logs (node):
  [stream-client] recv: 'data: Hello'
  (pause ~12s)
  [stream-client] recv: 'data: world'
  [stream-client] recv: 'data: !'
  (sometimes) ERROR: "socket hang up" or ECONNRESET after 30s idle

- Proxy logs (envoy) around timestamps: 
  [2026-02-25T12:14:32.123Z] "GET /v1/streams" 200 downstream_rq_completed
  [2026-02-25T12:14:44.456Z] upstream data paused: flow_control_window_exhausted
  (not consistent, sometimes absent)

- Server (runtime) internal logs:
  [2026-02-25T12:14:32.120Z] started stream id=xyz
  [2026-02-25T12:14:32.130Z] wrote chunk size=48
  [2026-02-25T12:14:32.131Z] wrote chunk size=35
  [2026-02-25T12:14:44.450Z] write error: EPIPE (connection closed by client)

Hypotheses / possible root causes:
- Proxy (envoy/nginx) buffering thresholds: small SSE chunks are being buffered until buffer or highwater mark reached, then forwarded in bursts (explain bursts).
- HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 translation at gateway: flow-control windows can pause forwarding until WINDOW_UPDATE arrives. If gateway mishandles WINDOW_UPDATE during long-lived streams, it may stall.
- Intermediary TCP GSO/TSO or Nagle interaction plus ACK coalescing causing latency spikes.
- Backpressure handling bug in runtime where write() returns EAGAIN but we treat as transient and retry later causing delays.
- Client-side keep-alive or read timeouts closing or pausing reads (unlikely: observed across curl/node/python).
- Load-dependent behavior: when backend overloaded, runtime batches output and flushes fewer, leading to large pauses.

Immediate mitigations to try (ordered):
1) Force larger chunk sizes from runtime (coalesce tokens into >1KB writes) to avoid proxy buffering heuristics. Quick change in runtime streaming writer.
2) Add explicit flushes and set 'X-Accel-Buffering: no' / 'Cache-Control: no-transform' / 'Connection: keep-alive' headers to hint proxies not to buffer.
3) Disable proxy buffering on envoy/nginx side for streaming routes. (Envoy: set "use_remote_address"/streaming configuration and make sure HTTP1/2 flow control enabled correctly.)
4) Add periodic SSE keepalive comments (':\n') every 10s as fallback to keep some proxies from closing idle connections.
5) Add telemetry in runtime to log last-write timestamps per-stream and upstream flush durations to correlate with proxy metrics.

Repro steps (minimal) to run locally and observe pauses:
1) Server: start runtime dev server (dev flags to enable streaming)
   ./bin/runtime --dev-streaming --port 8080 --model redwood-small
2) Client (curl SSE):
   curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" "http://localhost:8080/v1/streams?prompt=$(python3 -c 'print("x "*1000)')" 2>&1 | sed -u 's/^/CURL: /'
3) Proxy (optional) - run envoy locally with default config and route to 8080 to reproduce buffering behavior; compare direct vs through-proxy.

Notes for next steps / experiments to run:
- Reproduce with HTTP/2 client explicitly to see if behavior differs from HTTP/1.1. Use nghttp or curl --http2.
- Add an nginx config change to turn off proxy_buffering for streaming location and run A/B test.
- Instrument runtime to log return values of underlying socket write calls and any EAGAIN/EPIPE handling.
- Run a capture of envoy stats (flow_control_pending, stream_xx) while reproducing.
- Test with long but low-throughput streams (lots of small tokens) vs few large tokens to map threshold.

Questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the edge gateway configuration? (cc @Diego Martinez)
- Is there any cloud infra (LB) that performs HTTP/2->HTTP/1.x translation and could be misconfigured? (check GCP/ALB/CloudFront)
- Add a small integration test in repo that asserts per-token latency < 200ms for small tokens (maybe flaky but useful after fixes).

Scratch notes:
- Observed duplicate tokens likely from client reconnect + resume logic or a server retry that emits last N tokens again. Need to confirm whether resume logic exists in client.
- If buffering is due to upstream TLS termination/middlebox, then only change is to tune proxies or coalesce writes at runtime.

Attachments / links: see linked_artifacts for GH PR and JIRA. Will paste relevant logs into GH PR once I have a deterministic repro.

Quick trace example (timestamps):
- 12:14:32.130Z server write chunk1 48 bytes
- 12:14:32.131Z server write chunk2 35 bytes
- 12:14:32.132Z server write chunk3 40 bytes
- 12:14:44.450Z envoy forwarded all three chunks to client in one burst

End of notes.

-- Avery
